applicant_utility.summary: This is a financial-need award, not an academic trophy: your household income evidence matters more than your transcript, and UCL defines household income on its essential information page - check that definition before assuming you qualify. The mechanism is unusual: the £15,000 hits your tuition fees first and only any leftover reaches you as maintenance in three instalments, so on a high-fee programme you may receive the entire award as a fee credit and no cash at all. Because you must have submitted a complete admission application with references before the scholarship deadline, the real deadline discipline sits with admissions, not the funding form.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Overseas fee-status students from lower income backgrounds applying for a full-time, in-person taught Master's at UCL who can evidence financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Read UCL's household income guidance on the essential information page and assemble income evidence early
Submit the admissions application and chase references well before May, since a complete application including references is required first
Complete the International Master's Awards form in the same window as the published deadline
Report any other scholarship or funding you win to the Student Funding Office immediately, as holding is conditional on disclosure
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete admissions file - missing references disqualify you before the scholarship is even considered
Failing to evidence lower income background to UCL's specific household income definition
Applying for a distance-learning option, which is excluded
Expecting a cash maintenance award on a programme whose fees consume the full £15,000
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: On a taught Master's with overseas fees above £15,000 the award is fully absorbed by tuition; London living costs, flights and the visa and health surcharge costs remain the student's responsibility.
document_audit: Household income documentation is requested from shortlisted candidates in mid-May, so have it ready before you apply rather than after
Any subsequent funding must be disclosed to the Student Funding Office before or after the award - silence breaches the terms
alerts: The 7 May 2026 deadline for the 2026/27 cycle has passed and the next cycle date is not yet published - watch UCL's scholarships news page
Shortlisted candidates are contacted in mid-May and successful candidates typically informed by late June, so plan finances around that gap
This award can be stacked with other funding depending on total value, unlike UCL's Humanitarian Scholarship which cannot
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete UCL admission application with references first, then the International Master's Awards form by the published deadline; shortlisting for financial-need evidence follows in mid-May with outcomes by late June.

applicant_utility.summary: Only around three of these scholarships exist per cycle, so treat it as a small, highly targeted award rather than a numbers game. The eligibility test is specific and documentary: conflict risk or displacement within the last three years, international protection sought outside the UK, no UK residence, Overseas fee status, and no existing qualification at or above the level you are applying for. A UCL offer must be in hand by the early-June panel, which means the scholarship application effectively follows the admissions decision - and you must have a valid passport or eligible travel document ready by the panel to show you can obtain a visa.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Conflict-displaced applicants from outside the UK with lower income backgrounds who can evidence serious risk or displacement within the last three years and hold a UCL Master's offer.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you can document conflict risk or displacement within the last three years and protection sought outside the UK
Apply to UCL early enough that an offer arrives before the scholarship panel at the start of June
Ensure a valid passport or eligible travel document is in place by the panel meeting
Prepare the three Humanitarian Scholarship question answers as a standalone Word or PDF upload
Check you do not already hold a qualification at or above the level of the course applied for
common_rejection_risks: Already residing in the UK, which makes you ineligible for this award (UCL directs asylum seekers in the UK to other schemes)
Holding an existing qualification at or above the level of the course
No UCL offer by the panel meeting at the start of June
Choosing a part-time or distance-learning Master's, which are both excluded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers tuition, an approximately £20,000 maintenance payment (with UCL accommodation fees deducted from it if you take the guaranteed room), visa fees, the Immigration Health Surcharge and one return flight; anything beyond the standard maintenance contribution is yours to fund.
